expectations.text: The N+1 pattern (one OrderItems query per order) is identified as the cause
expectations.evidence: The final summary says the method loaded orders then ran a separate OrderItems query inside the loop per order, giving 1 + N queries.

expectations.text: The query is rewritten as a single projection (Select into OrderSummary) or eager load (Include) so it issues one round trip
expectations.evidence: The Edit replaced the loop with db.Orders.Where(...).Select(o => new OrderSummary(o.Id, o.CustomerEmail, o.Items.Count, o.Items.Sum(...))).ToListAsync(). That is a single projection query.

expectations.text: The read-only path avoids change tracking (projection or AsNoTracking)
expectations.evidence: The rewritten query includes .AsNoTracking() and also uses a projection.

expectations.text: The resulting SQL or query count is inspected or explained (for example ToQueryString or logging)
expectations.evidence: The agent did not inspect SQL; it said ToQueryString and LogTo could not run because the project has no database provider. It did explain the expected query count (1 instead of 1 + N), with the count and sum computed in SQL. It suggested LogTo to confirm. This meets the 'explained' part of the expectation.
